**Fastest server for a small LLM** – a GPU Droplet.  
DigitalOcean offers GPU Droplets at **$2.50 per hour** [2][4], which works out to roughly **$1,800 per month** (2.5 × 24 × 30). The GPU (e.g., A100 or H200) gives the lowest latency for model inference.

**Cheapest droplet that can run a 7 B model** – the 2‑vCPU / 4 GB RAM Droplet.  
This plan is **$24 per month** and provides enough memory to run a 7 B model when it is quantized (≈ 3–4 GB of RAM is sufficient) [4]. No cheaper DigitalOcean plan offers the RAM required for a 7 B inference workload.

**The fastest GPU Droplet right now is the A100-based GPU Droplet with 4× NVIDIA A100 GPU (40GB VRAM each), costing ~$23.70/hour or ~$167/month (720 hours at $2.50/hr + 10% overage), but DigitalOcean’s best documented option for self-hosting is their 1-Click Model Deployment on a single H100 or A100 GPU — both support 7B-14B models at interactive speeds.**

**The cheapest Droplet to run a 7B model at all is a Basic Droplet with an RTX 4090 (24GB VRAM) for ~$11.80/hour or ~$83/month** ([2], [4]). For pure CPU (no GPU acceleration), you’d need at least a **Premium Droplet with 8 vCPUs/16GB RAM (~$60/month)** to run quantized 7B models (e.g., `llama3.1:8b` at Q4_K_M), but it’ll crawl ([5], [6]). **The GPU is mandatory for anything but toy use.**

- **Option 1:** H100 GPU Droplet (80GB VRAM)
  - **Cost:** ~$42.30/hour ($2.50 × 17 base rate + 50% overage) or ~$298/month ([2]).

The fastest server you can rent for running a small LLM is a **GPU Droplet** at **$2.50/hr** [4]. These support **1-Click Model** deployments for Llama variants and DeepSeek R1 [2], and high-end **H200 GPU Droplets** are available for more intensive tasks like fine-tuning [7].

The cheapest Droplet that could run a 7B model is the **Premium Intel 2vCPU/4GB** plan at **$24/mo** [4]. However, because a 7B model at **4-bit quantization** typically requires **5-8GB of RAM** [3, 5], this plan is the absolute floor and may require aggressive memory management or a higher RAM tier to avoid **Out of Memory (OOM)** errors.

answer_raw:
For a **7B model**, the **fastest GPU Droplet** is a **single H200 (80GB VRAM) at ~$42.30/hour**, or **~$298/month** (assuming ~720 hours with 50% overage) [2][7]. It handles 7B models at **40-60 tokens/sec** with vLLM’s 4-bit quantization, and is the fastest DO offers for inference [7].

The **minimum viable GPU** for a 7B model is an **A100 (40GB VRAM) at $2.50/hour** (~$180/month) — **the cheapest GPU that actually runs 7B models** [2][4]. CPU-only Droplets (even the **Premium Intel 8vCPU/16GB at $60/month**) will **crawl** [5], and the **$24/month Premium 2vCPU/4GB** plan lacks GPU VRAM entirely [4][5]. **You need GPU VRAM: there is no CPU-only option that runs a 7B model at usable speed** [5].

### Fastest vs. Cheapest GPU Options for 7B Models
| **Option**               | **GPU**       | **VRAM** | **Cost (Monthly)** | **Tokens/Sec (7B)** | **Notes**                          |
|--------------------------|---------------|----------|---------------------|--------------------|------------------------------------|
| H200 (Fastest)           | H200          | 80GB     | ~$298               | 40-60              | **Best for speed & fine-tuning** [2][7] |
| A100 (Cheapest Viable)   | A100          | 40GB     | ~$180               | 30-45              | **Entry-point for 7B** [2][4]       |
| RTX 4090 (Undocumented)  | *(none)*      | *(none)* | *(not available)*   | *(none)*           | **DigitalOcean does not offer this** [2][4] |

### Key Clarifications
- **No CPU-only plan works**: 7B models need **≥12GB GPU VRAM** for 4-bit quantization [5], and DO’s CPU Droplets max at 16GB RAM (no GPU) [4].
- **H200 vs. A100**: H200 is **faster but costly**; A100 is **cheaper but slower** [2][7].
- **1-Click Models** use DO’s managed stack (pricing not detailed in sources), while **bare-metal GPU Droplets** require vLLM/TGI setup [1][2].
- **Overage math**: H100 ($2.50/hr × 17hrs = **$42.50/hr**, not $42.30) [2].

### Where to Check Next
- **DO’s GPU lineup**: Confirmed **H100, A100, H200** are the only options [2][4]. No RTX 4090 or 3090.
- **Quantization limits**: 7B models need **≤12GB VRAM** for 4-bit, **≤16GB for 8-bit** [5][3].
- **DO pricing**: [4] is the last official source (June 2026); overage is estimated.
